items.title: Deckers' Strong Balance Sheet Sets the Stage for Future Growth
items.summary: DECK leverages its strong cash position and financial flexibility to fund brand investments, reward shareholders and maintain disciplined spending.

items.title: Scott Galloway Is Buying Nike’s Dip. He Says Its Injury Isn’t “Career Ending”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysScott Galloway made the case for buying Nike on The Prof G Pod, calling its slump an injury that isn’t career-ending. Nike’s own plan has no return to market growth until fiscal 2029, and its 2031 targets still fall short of fiscal 2024’s results.

items.title: Why Is Nike (NKE) Stock Up Today? Dick's Strong Earnings Lift Retailers
items.summary: Nike shares rose 5.5% on Tuesday, Nov. 24, alongside Dick's Sporting Goods, which jumped after strong earnings, while the S&P 500 fell.

items.title: Nike Soars 6% as Competitor Calls US Foot Locker “A Particular Bright Spot”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysNike stock rose 6% today after Dick’s Sporting Goods said comparable sales at its US Foot Locker banner rose more than 4% last quarter. Nike is about 31% of what Dick’s buys, so a steadier Foot Locker supports the wholesale business Nike is rebuilding.

items.title: Nike Is Down About 80% From Its Peak and Just Told Investors Sales Will Fall Again
items.summary: Nike's stock has collapsed from its highs, analysts still show a 30% upside gap, and management just guided earnings far below what Wall Street expected. The math behind those price targets tells a very different story.

items.title: Deckers Outdoor (DECK) Stock Looks Cheap Following Its 2027 Sales Cut
items.summary: Deckers Outdoor has seen its share price come under pressure this year, and that slide puts fresh focus on a simple question for investors who follow the footwear group. Do the earnings that Deckers generates today, and the expectations tied to them, justify where the stock now trades? The share price is down 26.1% year to date, which raises the question of whether the current valuation is still in step with the business's earnings power. items.title: Nike Sinks 5%, Dick’s Sporting Goods Down 5% as Analyst Flags Jordan Allocation Cuts of Up to 50%
items.summary: Key TakeawaysNike fell 5% after an analyst said it plans to cut Jordan allocations to Dick’s Sporting Goods’ Foot Locker by up to 50%. Analysts already expect Nike’s revenue to fall to $42.

items.title: Nike Sinks 7% as Investor Day Warns Fiscal 2028 Will Be a “Challenging Year Financially”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysNike sank 7% today after saying fiscal 2028 adjusted EPS will fall modestly. Nike’s 2031 targets look cheap, but a down year comes first.
